name: comp-320

frames.best_why: Frame 6 shows the name fully typed and Delete switched on, the dialog's purpose in one still.

tagline: Delete dialog unlocks only after you type the project name exactly.
summary: A trigger opens a dark confirmation dialog with a warning icon and a name field. Delete stays dim until the typed text matches the project name exactly, then turns solid.
appearance: Closed, an outlined Delete project button. Open, a narrow dark rounded dialog centred on a warning circle, a bold Final confirmation heading, two centred grey lines naming coss-ui, a Project name label over a long outlined input, and a footer with equal Cancel and Delete buttons.
behaviour: Typing updates Delete: it stays dim and disabled until the value is exactly coss-ui, then becomes a white active button. Cancel closes the dialog; Delete itself does nothing.
demo_content: Delete project trigger; the dialog asks you to type coss-ui to confirm.
search_phrases: dialog that requires typing the name
use_when: A destructive action is serious enough that the user must type an exact name first.
avoid_when: The required project name is a constant in the file, so it must be edited for each use.
customise: The project name to type, all copy and the placeholder are hardcoded; the component accepts no props.
weight_why: One dialog and a text comparison; no animation beyond the opening fade.

a11y.note: The label is bound to the input and the icon hidden, but Delete has no handler and the unlock is not announced.

issues: Delete has no click handler, so confirming does nothing.
The name to type is a hardcoded constant rather than tied to a project.
polish_why: Clear, well-spaced confirm dialog with a satisfying unlock; the dead Delete action is the flaw.
